subject: Clearwave: model-riviera-2.0 P95 spike / SLA impact
messages:
From: Paul Rogers <paul@clearwave.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: eng-team@clearwave.com
Date: 2027-09-21T08:03:00-04:00
Subject: model-riviera-2.0 P95 spike — immediate SLA impact

Hey Aditya / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp P95 latency spike in our production traffic hitting model-riviera-2.0 starting ~07:45 ET this morning. Our monitoring shows p95 moving from ~190ms baseline to ~1.2s for a sustained 18-minute window across multiple regions. This is affecting our live claims-check workflow (time-sensitive).

Quick facts:
- Affected window: 07:45–08:03 ET
- P95 observed: 1.2s (avg baseline ~190ms)
- Sample request ids: rq_34f2, rq_34f5, rq_34fb (I've attached a CSV with the p95 time series we captured).
- Business impact: ~13% failure/timeout rate in our downstream processors while waiting on inference replies.

We are under an enterprise SLA that references p95 latency for inference (Section 3.2). We need immediate confirmation on:
1) Is this an isolated regression in model-riviera-2.0?
2) Can you switch our traffic to the last known stable variant (model-riviera-1.9 or 1.8) while you investigate?
3) If a rollback is required, what's the expected timeline and risk?

We can open a temporary maintenance window if you need it, but this is impacting customers. Please advise next steps and whether you need any additional logs from our side.

—Paul
Paul Rogers
Head of Engineering, Clearwave Health
paul@clearwave.com

Attachment: p95_timeseries.csv (CSV, 45KB)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Paul Rogers <paul@clearwave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-21T08:17:00-04:00
Subject: Re: model-riviera-2.0 P95 spike — immediate SLA impact

Paul — thanks for the details and the CSV, that helped. We're seeing the same signal in our telemetry for the customer tenant and a handful of other tenants in us-east-1. Preliminary notes:

- Symptom: P95 jump, tail latency outliers concentrated on sequences with long prompt prefixes; token-processing time per step increased for certain KV cache access patterns.
- Probable cause (initial): a model compile/kernel selection path that regresses on certain sequence-length distributions after the v2.0 build. Not yet confirmed — infra is pulling kernel logs now.

Immediate plan (provisional):
1) Roll traffic for Clearwave to model-riviera-1.9 variant as a canary fallback for your tenant only (no global impact). This is low-risk; variant is pinned in our catalog and has identical API semantics.
2) Apply a temporary traffic cap for short requests to reduce amplification while we investigate.
3) Collect a focused set of traces and the KV-cache access diffs — I'll attach the preliminary diff we pulled.

Can you confirm you approve the canary fallback for your traffic? If you prefer a full rollback to 1.9 for all traffic, we'll escalate but need leadership signoff.

Next steps on our side once you approve: execute canary, monitor for 10m, then either keep in fallback or open rollback window. I'll loop Marissa for contract/SLA coordination and Stephanie for approval for any wider rollback.

—Aditya Rao
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachment: prelim_riviera-diff.txt (text, 12KB)

Aditya — thanks for the quick triage. Marissa here (CS / account lead on Clearwave). A few points from the commercial side:

- Contract reference: Clearwave (CLW-12345) has a p95 latency SLA clause with credits outlined in Section 3.2. We should avoid issuing credits if we can remediate quickly (customer preference).
- Customer ask: tenant-only fallback to 1.9 immediately; would prefer not to have a full platform rollback.

Requesting formal approval for the tenant-scoped canary fallback and a provisional 2-hour SLA exception window where we can route their production traffic to 1.9 while root cause is identified. If this containment mitigates impact we can avoid an SLA credit and schedule a post-incident RCA.

I've attached the relevant contract excerpt for your review. If leadership approves, I recommend we:
1) Execute tenant fallback now (aditya to run).
2) Notify Clearwave that we are implementing a provisional exception for 2 hours and will provide periodic updates at 15-minute cadence.
3) If latency does not stabilize within 30 minutes of fallback, escalate to rollback authorization for broader audience.

Approve?

—Marissa Cole

Thanks team — provisional approval granted for a tenant-scoped fallback to model-riviera-1.9 for Clearwave and a 2-hour SLA exception window. Conditions:

1) Execute the fallback now and verify within 10 minutes that p95 for the tenant returns to baseline. If it does, keep the fallback in place and start a 2-hour monitoring window.
2) If p95 remains elevated after 30 minutes post-fallback, escalate to me immediately and I will authorize a broader rollback to 1.9 for impacted regions.
3) Legal: ensure the customer notification language is limited to incident mitigation and does not imply admission of breach. Marissa, please prepare the customer note.
4) Post-mortem: engineering to produce an RCA and performance regression test that demonstrates the fix before we consider rolling forward to 2.0.

Aditya — proceed with tenant canary switch, follow the monitoring/playbook runbook, and post updates every 15 minutes in the Slack thread linked below. If you need a broader rollback signature, ping me directly.

—Stephanie Nguyen
